rule.hypothesis: In the single positive case, a heavily commented, large WRONG_ANSWER candidate (comment_ratio ~0.86, code_chars ~21k) was followed by a CP run that passed all public tests, while the same candidate under P and G remained WRONG_ANSWER and a comment-stripped C run without the reminder produced a RUNTIME_ERROR. In the single unsuccessful case, a lightly commented, small WRONG_ANSWER candidate (comment_ratio ~0.26, code_chars ~1.4k) failed under CP, C, P, and G alike. This is consistent with, but does not establish, the cautious rule that comment stripping plus the fixed reminder may help mainly when the prior candidate is large and comment-heavy; otherwise keep the prior context. Only one positive and one unsuccessful source exist, so this is a weak, non-causal, non-transferable hypothesis.
rule.uncertainty: Based on exactly one positive and one unsuccessful public source; no causal certainty, no claim of broad safety or independent transfer. The thresholds are chosen to separate the two observed feature points (large/high-comment vs small/low-comment) and are not validated on unseen targets. The positive CP result could reflect the reminder, the stripping transform, or chance; the C RUNTIME_ERROR shows stripping without the reminder can be harmful. Outside the conjunctive scope the rule falls back to P (KEEP also uses P). No sealed results or unseen targets were provided.
